note: A demo pointing the retrieval question at Nestor's own decision memory: given every decision in docs/dogfood/decisions/, asked back, how well does the store answer, and when it is unsure what does it do? demo/the_dogfooding.py measures it three ways (verbatim, hand-authored paraphrase, and an authoring-free first-sentence sweep over the whole corpus), asserts every beat, and exits non-zero on drift like the sixty-second demo. The measurement turned up a real, already-open design question about the matcher the store is keyed with, filed as a draft rather than patched. Numbers below were produced by running it on this checkout (a 216-decision corpus including this file), not recalled; the demo re-measures live, so the corpus-size counts move as the store grows while the collision and paraphrase shapes hold.

decisions.question: An audit-memory demo owes 'how well does it retrieve', measured. How is that shown for the decision store without inventing or asserting numbers from memory?
decisions.commitment: demo/the_dogfooding.py reads the real docs/dogfood/decisions/*.json corpus (the same files scripts/dogfood_store.py ships, asserted equal to the committed decisions.json bundle), seals throwaway copies with a fixture key to exercise the serve path, and reports three measurements: verbatim self-retrieval (216/216 served, 0 wrong), ten hand-authored short paraphrases (2 served, 8 pending, 0 wrong), and an authoring-free sweep querying every multi-sentence question by its first sentence alone (50 questions: 4 served, 46 pending, 0 wrong). Every beat is a claim() that fails the build if it stops holding, exactly as demo/sixty_seconds.py and tests/test_demo.py already do.
decisions.why: The house rule that a near miss served as verified is worse than no answer is the whole product, and the honest way to demonstrate it is to point it at the product's own history and report the result whether or not it flatters. Three independent measures rather than one because the hand-authored paraphrases are the arguable part; the mechanical first-sentence sweep is the check that the paraphrase result is not a picked set. A demo that asserted these numbers from memory instead of producing them by running would be the exact failure the fixtures in demo/ exist to refuse.

decisions.question: The decision store keys prose-about-code with the default StringMatcher, but recipes/patch_review.py argues character similarity is the wrong scorer for that text. Swap in DefectMatcher, or leave it?
decisions.commitment: Leave it, and file the finding as a draft (IDEAS §6.94, open). Measured on the real corpus: StringMatcher admits two serve-bar collisions — §0051 and §0053, whose questions differ by one word ('The new gap assertions pass' vs 'The eight gap assertions pass') yet carry different committed answers, scored 0.94 — that DefectMatcher separates (zero collisions). But DefectMatcher's identifier-weighted keying also lowers paraphrase recall (2 of 10 to 1 of 10), and the shipped SEAL_THRESHOLD of 0.92 was calibrated for StringMatcher's character difflib, not for a score()-based matcher (nestor.memory emits a RuntimeWarning saying exactly this, which the demo catches and narrates rather than suppresses). So the choice is fewer-wrong-serves OR more-recall, and neither at the shipped bar without a per-matcher calibration.
decisions.why: A machine may propose and may not confirm, and the honest 'which matcher' answer needs a nestor calibrate --matcher run this session did not do — swapping the matcher silently would trade a measured failure mode (two nameable collisions) for an unmeasured one (recall loss at an uncalibrated threshold), which is the shape of unearned confidence this package exists to refuse. The finding is real and worth keeping, so it goes into the review desk as a draft, measured and re-measured by the demo on every run, for a human to decide.

decisions.question: Measuring what the store would serve needs sealed rows. Does the demo seal anything in the store that ships?
decisions.commitment: No. The committed docs/dogfood/nestor.db stays all-draft (dogfood_store.py seals nothing); the demo copies it to a temp directory, asserts the copy has zero sealed rows and serves None, and only seals throwaway copies elsewhere. tests/test_the_dogfooding_never_touches_the_committed_store snapshots docs/dogfood/ and fails if the run changed a byte of it.
decisions.why: The covenant is that nothing seals in the real store without a human at nestor.ui, and a demo about that covenant that quietly sealed its subject would be the covenant inverted. Copying-then-sealing keeps the shipped artifact untouched and provable, the same discipline demo/sixty_seconds.py and demo/two_desks.py already keep against a caller's own data.
